question: Should OpenClaw accept a broad tools.fs allowedPaths/denyPaths plus persisted subagent filesystem ceiling model in core, given exec remains outside this boundary and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/52951 is pursuing a different filesystem-roots design?
rationale: The code defects are concrete, but the permanent security/config shape and operator-facing promise require maintainer intent before this broad branch should be repaired or sponsored.

options.title: Require current-main security rework
options.body: Have the author rebase onto main, port PathGuard to agent-tools.ts, preserve restrictive-profile behavior, align generated schema, and provide runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Sponsor the PathGuard direction
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept the new allowedPaths/denyPaths and spawned-ceiling contract, document the exec limitation, and own the compatibility risk.

options.title: Pause for narrower filesystem-roots work
options.body: If the desired direction is the roots model, pause or close this broad branch and continue review on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/52951.

recommendation.title: Require current-main security rework
recommendation.body: Have the author rebase onto main, port PathGuard to agent-tools.ts, preserve restrictive-profile behavior, align generated schema, and provide runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about filesystem security boundaries and adjacent path-guard/media/apply_patch behavior where this history is strongest.
